long-term monitoring at catchment scale is essential for detecting changes in response to BMPs and to detect responses to changes in policy.

monitoring of water quality at the catchment level can provide useful information to farmers, regional councils and government agencies, and that long-term monitoring is required to detect changes in water quality in response to farmer action.

The main takeaway from our work is that

it is essential that monitoring of water quality in streams is carried out for a long period of time to be able to identify changes caused by farm management practices, and that the monitoring is at a catchment scale.
the adoption of BMPs can improve water quality in streams in pastoral dairy catchments, and that monitoring is required to detect the benefits of these actions.
long-term monitoring at a catchment scale provides a robust and reliable way to detect changes in water quality and to provide a sound basis for the development and implementation of effective BMPs.
